text:
Ava: Hey team — I pushed an RFC for attribute minimization + exporter routing for telemetry. tl;dr: strip direct PII (user_email, full_name), pseudonymize user_id & prompt_text via salted HMAC, and route sanitized spans to our public observability exporter while sending raw spans only to the secure/customer-owned exporter for Private accounts. @legal-bot please flag anything missing.

Raj: Quick Q — hash vs truncate? truncation is simple but leaks prefixes and makes dedupe harder. hashing preserves joinability if deterministic.

Mei: I'd vote HMAC-SHA256 with a per-customer salt stored in KMS. Deterministic HMAC lets us correlate a given user across requests without knowing the raw value. We must ensure salts are never exported.

Jordan: Salt rotation is a pain: when you rotate you lose the ability to join older spans unless we store salt_version on spans. Can we include a small telemetry.salt_version attr so backend can map?

Ava: good call — include telemetry.salt_version. Also thinking we should include telemetry.scrubbed=true and telemetry.scrub_policy=hash:user_id,prompt_text so consumers know it's been processed.

Raj: example exporter config for routing (working draft):

```
exporters:
  otlp_public:
    endpoint: https://otlp.public.redwood
    tags: ["sanitized"]
  otlp_secure:
    endpoint: https://otlp.secure.redwood
    auth: customer_kms
processors:
  scrubber:
    policies:
      - name: default
        remove: ["user_email","full_name"]
        hash: ["user_id","prompt_text"]
        salt_source: ksm://projects/...
  router:
    rules:
      - match: has_attribute("telemetry.sensitive", "true") -> otlp_secure
      - default -> otlp_public
```

Mei: a couple notes: (1) For prompt_text we should also prefix-truncate before hashing for very long prompts to avoid excessive compute and tokenization problems. (2) We should optionally keep a hashed prefix (first 128 bytes) + HMAC of full text.

Jordan: Ops/infra question — adding HMAC per-span will increase CPU. Can we batch HMACs for streaming requests or cache HMACs by request_id? We already have a request_id hash in KV cache.

Raj: Implementation plan: compute HMAC at ingestion boundary in C library (fast), add cache keyed by request_id for short TTL (5m) to avoid re-hashing identical requests. Also instrument a metric telemetry.scrub.cpu_seconds.

legal-bot: POLICY NOTE: hashed or pseudonymized values can still be considered personal data in some jurisdictions. Recommend: (A) treat hashed prompt_text as sensitive by default, (B) apply 90-day retention for pseudonymized prompt hashes in hosted mode, (C) prohibit sending raw prompt_text to third-party exporters unless customer explicitly opts in via Private deploy contract.

Ava: thanks. On retention: for Private customers who own exporter we can allow their retention rules, but for hosted default keep 90 days. We'll add a per-account retention_override flag for enterprise admins.

Mei: Sampling for high-cardinality attributes: default sample_rate = 0.01 for prompt_text hashes (1%), with reservoir counters so we can get accurate adjusted counts in metrics. Provide per-route overrides in console.

Raj: We should also add a "sensitive sampling" telemetry tag so routing rules can send a sampled subset to the public exporter but full copies to secure exporter for enterprise. Eg: telemetry.sensitive_sample=0.01.

Ava: UX question: console visibility. How do we show scrubbed values without leaking the raw? Proposal: show hashed preview (first 8 hex chars) + a label "redacted"; allow "Reveal" button only for accounts with audit access which triggers an audit log and requires 2FA.

Jordan: +1. Also require role-based gating for any UI-level reveal. Log must include who, when, and the span ids.

Mei: For debugging, developers often want short-lived access to full prompts. Could support ephemeral decrypt tokens for Private deployments that query KMS and require justification. Audit logged.

Raj: Edge case: cross-customer joins if two customers share same salt? should be impossible if salt is per-customer. Need to ensure hosted fallback salt is separate and non-deterministic per-tenant.

Ava: Decision proposal in-thread:
  1) Use salted HMAC-SHA256 for user_id & prompt_text.
  2) Include telemetry.salt_version, telemetry.scrub_policy, telemetry.scrubbed attrs on scrubbed spans.
  3) Default sampling for prompt hashes = 1% with per-route override.
  4) Route spans marked telemetry.sensitive=true to otlp_secure; otherwise public exporter.
  5) Hosted retention default = 90 days for pseudonymized hashes.
  6) Console shows hashed preview + reveal gated by RBAC + audit.

Raj: I'm good with that, will start a canary branch for the C lib and router rules.

Mei: I'll write the sampling/reservoir RFC and add tests for hash determinism.

Jordan: I'll update exporter runbook and add the new telemetry.scrub.cpu_seconds metric + alert if scrub CPU > 10% of ingestor CPU.

legal-bot: I'll confirm the retention language and the opt-in wording by Friday EOD.

Ava: Action items summarized: Raj: implement salt-version header + C lib canary. Mei: sampling defaults & tests. Jordan: exporter routing doc and alerts. Legal: retention text. I'll update RFC with the config snippet and link the PR.

Mei: ack.

telemetry-bot: Note — canary:router-rules v0.3 deployed to dev; metric telemetry.scrub.cpu_seconds is live.

Ava: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/492 (draft) — please review. :rocket: 

Jordan: quick nit — add a fallback policy for older spans missing salt_version: treat as legacy-hash:v1 and route to secure exporter by default.

Ava: done in RFC. Thanks all, closing thread unless anyone has blockers.

Raj: no blockers from runtime side.

legal-bot: will reply with exact phrasing.

Ava: great — merging in 48h if no objections. :thumbsup:
